user_correction: VectorTube should not be treated as a high-status core module. It is a simple sub-tool/example: a good example of how VectorFL can attach to another tool and expose only the needed VectorFL functions. VectorFL itself should eventually be attachable before/after many tools, enabling many AI usage patterns. Reverse-ontology was set up so VectorFL can grow in many directions rather than one predetermined direction.

corrected_positioning.VectorTube: small applied example / sub-tool / demonstration of partial VectorFL extraction
corrected_positioning.relationship: VectorTube = one tool-specific extraction of VectorFL capabilities, not the main target
corrected_positioning.analogy: VectorTube is like a plugin/use-case proving the attachment pattern, not the platform center

tool_attachment_model.before_tool: VectorFL can sit before a tool: interpret user direction, shape input, establish space/context/guards, decide what the tool should receive.
tool_attachment_model.after_tool: VectorFL can sit after a tool: read tool output, classify evidence/claim/action, mature it into space, route to Codex/Gemini/Hermes as needed.
tool_attachment_model.around_tool: VectorFL can wrap a tool: precheck → tool execution → receipt → layer reading → reentry.
tool_attachment_model.partial_extraction: A tool can use only needed VectorFL functions rather than the whole system.

reverse_ontology_role.why_it_exists: To prevent VectorFL from hardening around one direction/application/domain. The structure should let many possible directions emerge from use.
reverse_ontology_role.practical_meaning: Do not define VectorFL by VectorTube, YouTube, coding agents, or any single use-case. Each use-case reveals a reusable slice of VectorFL.
reverse_ontology_role.maturation_rule: When a sub-tool succeeds, extract the reusable VectorFL function and keep the tool-specific shell lightweight.

revised_asset_evaluation_note.previous_risk: VectorTube was being evaluated with too high a status, as if it were central.
revised_asset_evaluation_note.corrected_view: The valuable asset is not VectorTube itself but the attachment pattern it demonstrated: source/tool material → VectorFL mini-space/guard/inbox → Codex maturation path.
revised_asset_evaluation_note.what_to_promote_later: Promote reusable VectorFL functions/patterns, not the VectorTube shell.

implications_for_next_work: Asset typing should distinguish core VectorFL function from tool-specific adapter.
VectorTube artifacts should be tagged as ADAPTER_EXAMPLE / SUB_TOOL, not core authority.
Next asset map should add a dimension: core_function vs adapter_shell vs evidence_instance.
Reverse-ontology means multiple future adapters can exist: VectorTube, VectorGit, VectorDocs, VectorBrowser, etc., without forcing one canonical direction.
Codex maturation should recover the general pattern from each adapter and avoid overfitting to the adapter domain.

proposed_new_type_dimension.CORE_FUNCTION: Reusable VectorFL capability, e.g. layer reading, guard ring, space_inbox, evidence/provenance split.
proposed_new_type_dimension.ADAPTER_SHELL: Tool-specific packaging, e.g. VectorTube YouTube transcript runner.
proposed_new_type_dimension.MATURATION_SURFACE: Codex/Gemini/Hermes handoff or inbox surface that lets a function mature.
